case_title: Alamelu & Anr. v. State represented by Inspector of Police
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance/neighbour: one accused was a local boy about one kilometre from the victim's house, not related to or on visiting terms with her family; court noted no prior relationship. Prosecution alleged he had proposed marriage and she refused.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.366 (kidnapping/abduction to compel marriage); IPC s.376 (rape); s.376 and s.366 read with s.109 for accused Nos. 2 to 8
evidence_type: Oral testimony of victim, father, and cousin; medical and radiological age evidence (PW8, PW13); documentary school transfer certificate; police recovery and mahazar evidence
confession: None relied on. The prosecution alleged an accused told police they were married; the court did not treat this as a confession relied upon.
trial_court_outcome: All accused convicted under ss.366 and 376 (with s.109 for some); ten years rigorous imprisonment and Rs.500 fine each, default three months further RI
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; trial court conviction and sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: The victim, a young woman, was allegedly approached on a village road in the afternoon of 31 July 1993 by one of the accused, who said he loved her and wanted to marry her. She refused. A car then reached her and she was allegedly pushed into it by that accused, while other accused were already inside. A relative of the victim's family reportedly received a call from the accused about the abduction, and another relative reported it to the victim's father about an hour later. The father sent relatives to search, who reported that the victim could not be located, and a complaint was lodged with police two days later. The prosecution alleged that the next morning the victim was taken to a temple at a hill location, where one accused tied a mangalsutra around her neck despite her resistance. She was then allegedly kept in a house and repeatedly raped over three days. Relatives were allegedly present at the temple. The victim was recovered on 10 August 1993 from premises where the accused had stayed with her. Police seized a mangalsutra and clothing under mahazars. The victim was medically examined on 12 August 1993, and a radiologist and the examining doctor gave age ranges. The evidence included testimony from the victim, her father, a cousin, and a school transfer certificate giving a date of birth.
physical_harm: Alleged repeated rape; the judgment records no injury findings
number_of_offences: 2 charged (ss.366 and 376 IPC, with s.109 for accused Nos. 2 to 8); 0 finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Not found by the court; the court held the abduction story appeared concocted
motive: alleged: one accused wanted to marry the victim, who refused. The court did not accept this as an established motive.
key_evidence_accepted: Father's own admission at the panchayat that the daughter agreed to return after an hour; cousin's evidence that relatives were present at the temple; school transfer certificate and radiological age evidence were not accepted as proving minority
witness_credibility: Victim's testimony found unreliable and inconsistent, including on the abduction, the temple, and the house; father's testimony contradicted hers; relatives' evidence found unnatural. Expert age evidence did not rule out majority.
post_offence_conduct: Alleged: one accused took the victim to police and said they were married; she stayed with him until recovery on 10 August 1993. Court treated her conduct as inconsistent with coercion.
trial_duration: offence: 31 July 1993 (alleged); trial judgment: 28 April 2000; High Court: 6 February 2008; Supreme Court: 18 January 2011
legal_representation: Accused: R. Venkataramani, R. Ayyam Perumal, Aljo K. Joseph. State: S. Thananjayan
investigation_status: Complaint lodged 2 August 1993; FIR copy received 6 August 1993; accused arrested and victim recovered 10 August 1993; charge sheet filed 19 June 1996; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Transfer certificate marked only in 2000 after recall of victim; Headmaster who signed it not examined; no witness from the temple produced; High Court did not consider expert evidence on age variation
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted all accused. High Court: convictions affirmed. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, all accused acquitted.
prosecution_argument: Prosecution version was consistent; concurrent findings of the courts below on abduction and rape should not be disturbed under Article 136; father stated the victim was 15 years and 2 months old on 31 July 1993
defence_argument: Findings were perverse and ignored contradictions; there was no abduction, forcible marriage or rape; the story was false and the victim left home voluntarily; the complaint was lodged due to enmity
legal_principle_applied: Article 136 interference only where concurrent findings are manifestly perverse; benefit of doubt; date of birth in transfer certificate needs proof by a person who made the entry; victim's sole testimony may convict only if free from basic infirmities or improbabilities
precedent_relied_upon: Birad Mal Singhvi v. Anand Purohit, 1988 (Suppl.) SCC 604; Narbada Devi Gupta v. Birendra Kumar Jaiswal, (2003) 8 SCC 745; Jaya Mala v. Home Secretary, Government of J&K, (1982) 2 SCC 538; Ravinder Singh Gorkhi v. State of U.P., (2006) 5 SCC 584; Rameshwar v. State of Rajasthan, (1952) SCR 377
other_sentence_order: Accused directed to be released forthwith
